cards.anchor: Exactly K2, K5 and K7 checked, all other keys unchecked, no incorrect-key write, read-only scores preserved, latest snapshot loaded and completion within ten simulated minutes.
cards.burden: Hypothesized completion costs eight simulated minutes: three selections, three commits, one refresh and one final inspection. Requires a manual key checklist and complete action/write log; operational savings and human benefit remain unmeasured.
cards.construction: Keep stipulated row binding and loaded S0. Inspect/select K2 during 0-1 and commit during 1-2; select K5 during 2-3 and commit during 3-4; select K7 during 4-5 and commit during 5-6. Refresh only during 6-7 to load S2, preserving local statuses by key. Inspect keys and statuses during 7-8 for acceptance. Do not refresh inside inspections or use a correction loop.
cards.defeat: Reject if any actual write targets another key, even if repaired; the final map differs from the target map; source scores are edited; S2 is not loaded; or elapsed time exceeds ten. Such failure defeats this candidate completion, although its cause requires separate diagnosis.
cards.mutation: Move refresh from the selection-to-commit interval to a single boundary after all status writes; use immutable keys in the final acceptance scan, including equal-score K5 and K7.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis: S0 keeps selected rows 2, 5 and 7 stable through their commits, so the only writes are K2/K5/K7 checked. The final refresh loads S2 without changing those key-associated statuses, yielding accepted completion by minute eight.
cards.prediction_rival: The per-commit-refresh necessity account predicts this schedule cannot reliably achieve the unchanged valued outcome because every commit omits its claimed prerequisite. Verified success would refute that necessity within the synthetic model.
cards.probe: Replay once from all-unchecked S0 with the declared eight-minute schedule. Record action times, loaded snapshots, retained rows, intended keys and every actual key/value write. Independently compare the final key/status map, unchanged source scores and loaded S2 with the acceptance conditions. A final-only snapshot check cannot erase an earlier wrong-key write.
cards.rival: Reliable fixed-key corrections require refreshing immediately before each commit; final freshness alone is insufficient.
unknowns: No completed replay is supplied; the predicted success remains hypothetical.
Real selection binding, detection rates and interruption costs are unknown.
Concurrent status changes, deleted keys and snapshot-load failures are outside the model; one stipulated miswrite does not establish recurring feedback.

cards.anchor: Achieve the same exact-key correction, zero wrong-key writes, read-only scores, latest-snapshot compliance and ten-minute limit while retaining refresh immediately before each commit.
cards.burden: The candidate uses the available simulated immutable-key control and costs exactly ten minutes including final inspection: three selections, three refreshes and three commits, plus acceptance inspection. No time margin or production implementation is established.
cards.construction: Hypothesize immutable-key selection binding using R5. Select K2 during 0-1, refresh 1-2, commit 2-3; select K5 during 3-4, refresh 4-5, commit 5-6; select K7 during 6-7, refresh 7-8, commit 8-9. Inspect final keys/statuses during 9-10. Retain each selected key across reordering and write its checked status; identify targets by key rather than score.
cards.defeat: A changed target key across refresh or any wrong-key commit defeats the binding mechanism. Any incorrect final map, edited score, missing S2 or elapsed time above ten defeats completion. Do not repair errors and count the repaired run as successful.
cards.mutation: Change the selection interface from retained row number to retained immutable key, preserving the refresh schedule and score ordering.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis: changing/frozen snapshots crossed with row/key binding produce a first K5 write only in changing-plus-row; the other three diagnostic arms write K2. The separate changing-plus-key completion writes only K2/K5/K7, loads S2 and passes acceptance at minute ten despite the score tie.
cards.prediction_rival: The timing-only account predicts that identical refresh timing remains sufficient to induce the wrong target even with key binding. Its prediction differs specifically in the changing-plus-key arm.
cards.probe: Use separate diagnostic replays of select 0-1, refresh 1-2 and commit 2-3 in all four R5 controls, holding sorting, target and actions fixed. Log retained identity and actual writes. Then reset to all-unchecked S0 and execute the declared ten-minute changing-plus-key completion. Frozen diagnostic arms are mechanism controls, not final-freshness successes.
cards.rival: Snapshot/refresh timing alone accounts for the error; selection binding does not separate correct from wrong-target commits under the same changing-snapshot schedule.
unknowns: The key-bound control is available only as a stipulated synthetic intervention; real editor support is unknown.
Both diagnostic predictions and the ten-minute completion require executed traces.
This does not establish mismatch-triggered recurrence, usability benefits or robustness to omitted concurrency/failure conditions.
